speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness, specifically how long they last and what your movements look like? I also need to know if you have any awareness of these events afterward or if you experience any triggers like stress or lack of sleep.

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have a history of head trauma, febrile seizures, or any known neurological conditions? I would also like to know if these episodes occur during sleep or are strictly daytime events. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG findings and the specific aura of a "muddy taste" strongly point toward right temporal lobe epilepsy. I would like to request further imaging to rule out any structural abnormalities. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation and EEG findings are highly suggestive of right temporal lobe epilepsy, but I need to rule out a structural cause. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI rules out structural causes, confirming the diagnosis of focal impaired awareness seizures secondary to right temporal lobe epilepsy. Do you have any questions regarding the initiation of antiepileptic medication or lifestyle modifications to prevent triggers?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and characteristic EEG findings, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right temporal lobe epilepsy
